segments: 482 Book of the Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
The Great Kingdom was ruled on account of Queen Tōregene.
And in that vicinity, when Güyük Khan arose to go to the western countries,
and reached a certain place only seven days' march distant from the city of Beshbalik,
his end overtook him.
Now, some of the nobles of the Romans also wished
that the middle son of Ghiyath al-Din,
who was Rukn al-Din,
should reign.
And when the vizier Shams al-Din Isfahani perceived this,
he seized all of them {OCR?}
and killed them.
And he became haughty in his own eyes,
and took the mother of Sultan Izz al-Din as wife,
and begot a son by her.
And this shameful deed was displeasing in the eyes of everyone.
And when he had prepared much gold, and royal vessels, and horses, with the middle son Rukn al-Din,
he also sent him to the Tatars,
as we have said,
for the confirmation of peace.
When that youth reached Güyük Khan,
one of the nobles who were with Rukn al-Din,
who was Baha al-Din the Dragoman (interpreter),
slandered the vizier before the Khan, [saying]:
"He has killed the nobles,
and has taken the wife of the deceased sultan,
and has decreed and set up a new sultan without your command."
Then the Khan commanded
that Izz al-Din should step down from the throne,
and Rukn al-Din, who had seen our face, should reign;
and Baha al-Din the Dragoman should become his vizier,
and Shams al-Din should be dismissed.
And when they turned their face to come [back],
that vizier heard and trembled,
and sent Rashid al-Din the subashi of Melitene,
who was then Amir al-Arid,
with much gold and fine coins,
to go to the Khan
and bring him a confirmation of the decree.
And when this man reached Erzincan, he heard that they were close to arriving,
[namely] Sultan Rukn al-Din and Baha al-Din the Dragoman.
And when he was afraid,
he took the treasure that was with him up to the fortress of Kamach,
while he, with lightly equipped men, fled to Aleppo.
And after a little [while], Baha al-Din arrived,
and with him were two thousand Mongols.
And Rukn al-Din was proclaimed sultan in Erzincan, Sebastia, Caesarea, Melitene, Hisn Ziyad, and Amid.
And new governors and prefects were established in every place,
and those of Izz al-Din were dismissed.
